details.description: The medical_conversation model is a Google Cloud Speech-to-Text V1 model tailored for transcribing dialogue between a medical provider, such as a doctor or nurse, and a patient. Google's documentation states words spoken by each speaker are automatically detected and labeled in the returned transcript, and the model is available only for en-US audio. Google's Speech-to-Text V1 docs recommend that new users use the V2 API instead, though medical_conversation is a V1-specific model.
advantages: Automatically detects and labels which speaker (provider or patient) said each part of the transcript, per Google's documentation.
Supports automatic punctuation, alternate transcriptions, word timestamps and word-level confidence scores.
disadvantages: Only available for en-US audio, per Google's documentation.
Is a Speech-to-Text V1 model; Google's documentation recommends new Speech-to-Text users use the V2 API instead.
use_cases: Transcribing conversations between a medical provider and a patient, such as clinical visits

notes: Source page gives no WER/accuracy figures and no explicit GA/deprecated status; Speech-to-Text release notes (docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/release-notes) show medical models launched Nov 8 2021 with no later deprecation notice found, so the model is treated as current.
